enrichments.summary: The FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine and Human Foods Program issued a final guidance document detailing best practices for convening a GRAS panel. The guidance provides recommendations for proponents of GRAS status on how to identify qualified panel members with appropriate expertise, manage potential conflicts of interest, and ensure the panel's evaluation relies on publicly available information to establish that a substance is safe for its intended use in human or animal food.
key_regulations: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act)

enrichments.summary: This filing represents a formal amendment to GRAS Notice (GRN) 1261 regarding the safety and intended use of 2'-Fucosyllactose (2'-FL) as a food ingredient, typically targeting infant formula and medical food applications.
FDA has received GRAS Notice (GRN) 1284 regarding the use of recombinant bovine lactoferrin, produced by a modified strain of Komagataella phaffii, as a food ingredient.

The FDA received an amendment to GRAS Notice 1220, which concerns the safety notification for mycelial biomass derived from the Phoenix Oyster mushroom (Pleurotus pulmonarius) for use as a food ingredient.

The FDA issued a guidance document detailing recommendations for the submission of chemical and technological data to support food additive petitions and GRAS notices for enzyme preparations used in food processing. It covers the required identity and characterization of enzymes and their sources, manufacturing processes, purity specifications, intended technical effects, dietary exposure estimates, and specific provisions for use in meat, poultry, egg products, and potential food allergens.
key_entities: Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition

enrichments.summary: The FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) issued a final guidance document detailing the safety and effectiveness data needed to determine if nonprescription (OTC) sunscreen active ingredients are Generally Recognized as Safe and Effective (GRASE) under the Sunscreen Innovation Act.
key_entities: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research

enrichments.summary: The FDA issued a Guidance for Industry on how manufacturers of food ingredients and food contact substances should assess the effects of significant manufacturing process changes, such as adopting emerging technologies like nanotechnology, on a product's safety and regulatory status.

The FDA (CDER) issued a final guidance document detailing recommendations for designing and conducting Maximal Usage Trials (MUsT). These in vivo absorption trials are used to assess the bioavailability of topically applied active ingredients being considered for an over-the-counter (OTC) drug monograph to determine if systemic exposure requires additional safety data for a GRASE determination.
key_entities: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research

enrichments.summary: The FDA issued a Small Entity Compliance Guide to help businesses comply with the final rule for OTC topical acne drug products. The rule officially classifies benzoyl peroxide as a Generally Recognized as Safe and Effective (GRASE) active ingredient, mandates specific new warnings and directions for its use, and updates labeling requirements for all OTC topical acne products to align with the standardized Drug Facts formatting under 21 CFR 201.66.
key_entities: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research

enrichments.summary: The FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine (CVM) issued final guidance GFI #262, which details the recommended information and procedures for pre-submission consultations prior to submitting animal food additive petitions (FAPs), Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) notices for animal food, and Food Use Authorization (FUA) requests.
Middlefield Original Cheese Co-op and Copia Collective are recalling 100% Grass-Fed Pepper Jack Cheese products due to potential contamination with Listeria monocytogenes.

The FDA has issued a notice requesting public comments on its information collection activities concerning Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) notifications and the process for convening panels related to GRAS substances. This is part of a routine Office of Management and Budget review process.
Goldenroot is recalling its Yuzu Ginger Lemongrass Ginger Beer because it contains ginger juice that was not properly pasteurized, posing a potential safety risk.
FDA has received amendments to GRAS Notice (GRN) 1269 concerning the use of modified-monellin preparation as a food ingredient.

The FDA received amendments to GRAS Notice (GRN) 1260 regarding Rebaudioside M. This filing is part of the regulatory process for establishing the 'Generally Recognized as Safe' status for the ingredient when used as a sweetener in food products.

The FDA issued a Small Entity Compliance Guide to help small businesses comply with the Consumer Antiseptic Wash Final Rule (81 FR 61106). The rule finalizes the nonmonograph status of 19 active ingredients, including triclosan and triclocarban, declaring them not Generally Recognized as Safe and Effective (GRASE) for use in OTC consumer antiseptic washes. Benzalkonium chloride, benzethonium chloride, and chloroxylenol were deferred from the final rule to allow sponsors more time to submit necessary safety and effectiveness data.
key_entities: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research

enrichments.summary: The FDA is requesting public comments on proposed information collection activities pertaining to substances generally recognized as safe (GRAS) notifications and the process for convening panels related to these substances. The comment period closes on August 26, 2025.

FDA Compliance Policy Guide (CPG) Sec 500.200 outlines enforcement policies for GRAS food additives. The guidance clarifies that foods containing GRAS substances may be deemed adulterated if the substance is not of food grade, exceeds the amount reasonably required to accomplish the intended technical effect, or violates Good Manufacturing Practices.

The FDA issued a warning letter to Revitalize Energy, Inc. for marketing 'Revitalize Energizing Eye Drops' as an unapproved new drug and misbranded drug. The product contains active ingredients (menthol, camphor, caffeine, taurine) not permitted under the OTC monograph for ophthalmic drugs. The product's labeling includes unapproved claims, such as treating 'screen fatigue' and protecting against cataracts, and improperly uses the FDA logo to imply approval or compliance.
key_entities: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER)

enrichments.summary: The FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research issued a final guidance document detailing the procedures for industry sponsors to withdraw 586A requests or pending requests under the Sunscreen Innovation Act. These requests seek determinations on whether nonprescription sunscreen active ingredients are Generally Recognized as Safe and Effective (GRASE) for use in over-the-counter (OTC) sunscreen monographs.
key_entities: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research

enrichments.summary: Live it Up brand Super Greens dietary supplement powders are being recalled due to potential contamination with Salmonella Typhimurium.

The FDA has received a GRAS notice (GRN 1165) for (R)-1,3-Butanediol, a substance intended for use as an ingredient in conventional foods. This filing represents a manufacturer's self-affirmation of safety which the FDA will review for any concerns.
key_regulations: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act

enrichments.summary: The FDA issued final guidance detailing the regulatory framework for GRAS substances in human and animal food, encouraging industry to submit GRAS notices and warning that non-GRAS substances used without approval are unsafe food additives subject to enforcement.

The FDA issued updated final guidance providing answers to Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding the regulatory process and considerations for classifying substances intended for use in human or animal food as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS).
key_entities: Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition (CFSAN)

enrichments.summary: Live it Up brand Super Greens dietary supplement powder is being recalled due to potential contamination with Salmonella Typhimurium.

The FDA has initiated a comprehensive re-assessment of butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA), a common food chemical preservative, and issued a Request for Information (RFI) to gather data on its safety and use. This action is part of a broader effort to review chemical additives in the food supply, with the potential to remove BHA if it does not meet current safety standards. BHT and azodicarbonamide are also slated for future assessments. The FDA is also reforming its GRAS framework.
